oracle: For each row-major RGB pixel: floor((77*R + 150*G + 29*B + 128)/256), unsigned bytes, LSB-first.
checks: Strict actual expressions, references, state initial values, numeric event dispatch order, public ports, statistics and structural MD5; no extra nodes.
Real FIFO interpreter; each frame stores all input before scheduling, executes exact finite token waves, selects each saved RGB pixel in turn and checks every conditional output-state write.

Each frame executes 2791 steps, nine rounds and nine publications per output bit; idle caches contain only nine C tokens. Actual sequential JK operation counts equal counts derived from the validated execution schedule.
10,000 random frames by default plus all 256 equal-RGB values, all 216 one-hot/one-cold vectors, boundaries, repeats, each individually missing input and staged/non-drained input sends.
Initial bootstrap, reset after complete/partial/computing frames and file reread/recompilation during computation restore declared state and the two-step idle initialization.
A full first frame sent before draining Bootstrap also completes correctly; callers do not need a separate initialization drain.
termination_argument: The checked expressions restrict the only feedback to CoreDone -> C -> Ti, Ti -> M(i+1), T8 -> Tick, selector state, and output-state readback. Arithmetic is a forward-only stateless DAG; output self-publication cannot enqueue without a fresh core-bit arrival.

One complete frame publishes FrameSeed exactly once. M0 consequently publishes once, so T0 consumes at most one M0 token. Mi receives one FrameSeed event and one event per T(i-1) publication; therefore Ti publishes at most i+1 times. T8 can produce at most nine Tick events, regardless of input values. This is a structural finite-event bound, not a conclusion inferred from a step timeout.

From the checked idle marking (one C arrival cached at every Ti), FIFO order generates token waves [T0..T8], [T1..T8], ..., [T8]. Each Tick advances the selector, reads one pixel, runs the arithmetic DAG, writes all 72 output states and then publishes CoreDone. C replenishes the token slots; each successive wave is one token shorter. After wave nine there are no remaining M arrivals, and only nine cached C arrivals remain.

The exact per-frame bound and successful schedule comprise 216 storage executions, one FrameSeed, 45 M, 45 T, nine C, nine Tick, 81 selector-state, 216 selected-input, 1512 arithmetic-core, 648 output-state and nine CoreDone executions: 2791 total. Initialization is separate: Bootstrap then C, two executions.
boundary: Sampled 216-bit frame domain using actual JKEngine.send/step. Every Xi appears once per frame; disjoint partial sends and stepping between sends are allowed. A new frame starts only after the preceding frame completes and returns to the idle token marking. Each output bit publishes nine times per frame, retaining its preceding value until its pixel round. The complete 72-bit result is valid after all nine rounds, not atomically before then. No claim covers overlapping frames, duplicate input sends within a frame, arbitrary initial state, all 2^216 input combinations, external hardware, browser integration or global node-count optimality.
